description: Four-panel composite of optical micrographs (etched, bright-field) at the same magnification, labelled (a)-(d) in the top-left of each panel, each carrying a 50 μm scale bar in its bottom-left corner. (a) M1-SS and (b) M1-30 are the solution-treated and 30 h aged conditions of the M1 steel: coarse equiaxed austenite grains with straight annealing-twin lamellae and thin dark grain boundaries; the two fields look essentially identical in grain size and morphology, showing that 30 h aging does not visibly alter the equiaxed grain structure at this magnification, although sparse dark particles are present. (c) M2-SS and (d) M2-30 are the Ti- and V-added M2 steel, whose equiaxed grains are visibly finer and more numerous per field of view; both panels contain a much higher density of fine dark second-phase particles decorating grain boundaries and grain interiors, and this particle density is clearly higher in the aged condition (d) than in the solution-treated condition (c). The figure's argument: adding Ti and V refines the austenite grain size and produces abundant fine precipitates, while 30 h aging leaves the equiaxed grain morphology of both steels unchanged. No grain-size numbers are printed on the micrographs.

subfigures.description: Optical micrograph of M1-SS (solution-treated M1 steel) with 50 μm scale bar: coarse equiaxed austenite grains with straight annealing twins and thin dark boundaries.
Optical micrograph of M1-30 (M1 steel aged 30 h) with 50 μm scale bar: equiaxed grain structure very similar in grain size to (a), with a few dark particles.
Optical micrograph of M2-SS (solution-treated Ti- and V-added M2 steel) with 50 μm scale bar: visibly finer equiaxed grains and a dense dispersion of fine dark particles.
Optical micrograph of M2-30 (M2 steel aged 30 h) with 50 μm scale bar: fine equiaxed grains with an even higher density of fine dark particles along grain boundaries and interiors.

observations.observation: The figure contains four optical micrographs, each labelled (a)-(d) in the top-left corner and each with a 50 μm scale bar in the bottom-left corner.
Panels (a) and (b) show coarse equiaxed grains with straight annealing-twin lamellae and thin dark grain boundaries; the two fields have essentially the same grain size.
Panels (c) and (d) show visibly finer equiaxed grains with a markedly higher density of fine dark second-phase particles than panels (a) and (b).
Within the M2 steel, the aged panel (d) shows a higher density of fine dark particles than the solution-treated panel (c).
The caption identifies the panels as the metallographic structure of (a) M1-SS, (b) M1-30, (c) M2-SS, (d) M2-30.

The citing text states that Fig. 1 (a) and (b) are the solution-treated and 30 h aged conditions of M1 steel, both exhibiting equiaxed grain morphology, with no significant grain-size change after aging (average 45.3 ± 9.3 μm).
The citing text states that Fig. 1 (c) and (d) show M2 steel in solution-treated and 30 h aged conditions with equiaxed grains of average size approximately 32.3 ± 10.4 μm.
The citing text states that, compared with M1 steel, the Ti- and V-added M2 steel shows significantly refined grain size.

The citing text states that thermodynamic calculations of phase composition confirm the matrix remains single-phase austenite after aging treatment [39]; the micrographs themselves show no second-phase matrix transformation.
The citing text states that the grain sizes of M1 and M2 are listed in Table 2 of the paper.
No grain-size value, magnification figure or axis scale is printed inside any of the four micrographs; only the 50 μm scale bars are visible.
